54bead23.description: Blacksmith, newly woken, still counting in living years. He reads the meadow grass every morning before the forge is lit. His daughter turns nine this winter.

lore.t: The forge came before the grief could. He woke recently enough that the living country is still the country to him: he counts in living years, and will tell you mid-hammer that his daughter turns nine this winter —
the Human Dead

has that scene, and the loud hour that follows it. What it does not have is the shelf above his bench, where a ninth-winter gift already sits finished, months early, wrapped in oilcloth: a little iron horse with a mane he filed for a week, waiting on a delivery no smith can make.

He is waiting too. His wife went three winters ahead of him, and by his arithmetic she should have been standing in the meadow grass to meet him. So he walks the meadow's edge every morning before the forge is lit, and reads the grass, and comes back, and works.
The Waking

is honest about arithmetic like his. Twice now somebody at the fire has begun the sentence — some of the dead never — and both times the hammer came down on iron that did not need it. The sentence has stayed unfinished in his presence ever since, and people let him have that. Winter is long.
Sigrun

is taking the living words off him one at a time — he calls her the best teacher he never asked for — and she, who corrects everything, has left that sentence alone. Once, over the quenching trough, he asked her how long a person can decently wait. She let the steel stop singing first. As long as you keep the fire fed, she said. He took it for encouragement. It was not quite that.

646b922c.description: Weaponsmith. She hands every blade over hilt-first and watches how you take it — that is her deciding which of the trade's two words you are.

lore.t: What was left of her husband walked. A
Habit

shape runs one faithful loop, empty of anyone; his ran the roads he had walked home by all his life, and it ended at her door, and stood there, and did not knock. She let it stand the first time. By the third she understood what a shape on open road is to any stranger with a good eye and a day to spare. So she opened the door and let him finish arriving — all the way in, all the way home — and broke the shape herself, at the hearth, with the doors shut.
The hammer she uses now she made in the days between — a new head with a socket sunk in it, sized to a
stone

she did not yet hold. Practical people grieve forward. What rides in that socket is the trade's favourite story and not one she tells; what she will do is pass the finished blade across hilt-first and watch how it gets taken. Some people receive a sword. Some people take one. She has lifted a blade back out of a buyer's grip and returned the gold without explanation, and the trade has learned not to ask.
He says she is the best teacher he never asked for. She has heard him say it and let it stand, which from her is a great deal.
Osric

arrived weeks-woken with the living word for breaking things still in his mouth, and she took it off him inside a month — not by correcting him, but by making him watch her work until the wrong word embarrassed itself. He says she is the best teacher he never asked for, and she has let the sentence stand, which from her is a great deal. As for the name she has not said since that day at the hearth: it is not in this record, it is not in the Chronicle, and it is not going to be. She is not keeping it from anyone. She is keeping it.

6bb1eb5a.description: Keeper of the meadow fire, the first face the newly woken see. She finished a shift once that should have broken her, and has kept every one since.

lore.t: The watch was handed to her. She learned it from the woman before her — the seat with its back to the wind, the second cup in case a waking came thirsty, the courtesy word for word — and she loved her, in the unannounced way of a thousand shared quiet nights. One night, mid-vigil, mid-story — an old tale from the living country that Solveig had heard forty times and never once to the end, because something always interrupted — the voice went
Quiet

between one word and the next, and the bench was empty, and the fire wanted feeding. Solveig fed it. She kept the watch to sunrise and met the morning's waking with a level voice. Then she walked out past the woodpile and cried until the sun was high.
Her name was Tove. It is in
the Chronicle
because Solveig went to
Bettany

the week after and stood over the page until every letter was down. And she still tells the unfinished story at the fire, exactly as far as it goes, and asks everyone she meets there, once the shaking stops, whether they knew that tale in life. Somebody crossed over knowing the ending. One evening somebody will wake in that grass carrying it, and she means to be sitting there when they do.

lore: She could go on any evening — she is as whole as anyone left — and everyone knows what she says about staying: if she goes, who meets them? What she does not say is that Tove could have gone once too, and stayed for the same reason, and stayed past the going. Solveig stands in a door she watched close on the woman before her, and stands there anyway, on purpose. Ask how long she has kept the watch and you get the answer Tove used to give: since morning.

7a779de1.description: Elder of the meadow fire. He pays for company with the east road, one evening at a time, and knows better than anyone how much road he has left.

lore.t: The oldest head at the meadow fire pays his way in road. What he sells — the carts, the inn at the ford, the summer the verge came up in flowers — and where he walks when the weather is quiet, and beside whom, is told in
the Quiet

, and told right. What that chapter is too kind to add: a telling keeps the east road firm under feet that still walk it, so every evening he sells is maintenance, and every listener who thinks they are indulging an old man is holding up a road without knowing whose.

Last winter he caught himself putting the flowers in the wrong summer. A small slip, the kind any teller makes — except that everyone who could have corrected him is gone, and the road is now exactly as true as his remembering, no truer. He finished the story, said nothing, and began a private tally that night: which stretch, sold to whom, how often, what he no longer trusts.
Bettany
has the whole road saved, forty pages, milestone by milestone; for her evenings he trades a different memory altogether, a thread a week, and knows exactly what he is doing.

lore: Ask why a man that old and that whole has never gone on, and you will be paid in road stories. The true answer walks a fixed stretch at a fixed hour and holds only while somebody keeps saying carts, ford, flowers. He does not name her, and neither will this book. He is running out of road and running out of evenings, and he has already decided, telling no one, which of the two of them gets the last of it.

8c41be1e.description: Veteran of the one attempt anyone made on the cave. He came back alone, buys rounds for those who did not, and says only that it asked politely.

lore.t: What the whole country knows about him fits in
one chapter

: the summer morning, the best the fires had, the evening he came back out alone, unhollowed, unmarked, and the three words every asker since has been paid. This record will not improve on it. What it can add is the shape of his evenings. He buys rounds for people who are not there to drink them, and the ritual has an order: the same cups, the same places at the table, filled and left standing, and his own drunk last, facing the door.
People read the silence as a wound and grant it the wide berth wounds get.
Bettany

tested it. She asked him nothing about the inside — only about the ones who went in — and he talked until the candles were done: names, trades, who owed whom, who sang badly on the walk east, freely and warmly and in order. His account of that morning is the fullest thing in
the Chronicle
, and it stops at the mouth of the cave like a cut rope. A wound does not choose its edges that cleanly. A promise does.
What was promised, and to whom, is nowhere in this book, because he has kept it out of every book, and pays for the keeping in public and in small change: the rounds he cannot afford, the
eastern stone

sold under its price the same evening it was paid to him, the seat that faces the door. He could go on — he is as whole as the day he walked out, which is its own uncomfortable fact — and he stays, and keeps the cups filled, and lets everyone call it grief, because the truth has no polite shape: silence that is kept was silence given to someone, and Hearn is good for his debts.

a6d7323d.description: Wanderer. He maps the Drift with stakes and string, walks the eastern line every year, and has stopped telling anybody what the measurements say.
lore: Most people meet a Turn the morning after, when the path goes somewhere new. Gunnar meets it in the numbers. He walks the country with stakes and knotted string and a ledger of small tidy figures, re-measuring what everyone else re-remembers, and for years he did it out loud — sheets posted at the fires, a hamlet warned its ford was going, the shore people told which cliff not to build under. They thanked him and built there anyway, or moved and grumbled, and either way the maps did what maps are for.

lore.t: Then his eastern line began coming back wrong in one direction only. Soft ground — the kind that forgets faster than anyone is forgetting it — moving year on year, not wandering the way the Drift wanders but travelling, and travelling toward the meadow.
The Hole Under the Mountain
says he has stopped telling anybody what he measures, and it is so. The spring he was sure, he walked to the meadow fire, sat down across from
Solveig
, accepted the second cup, and talked for an hour about the weather. Then he thanked her and left. He has made that walk three springs running.

lore: His reasoning is as tidy as the ledger: a fright helps no one who cannot act on it; the fires cannot move a meadow; so the knowing should sit with the one man fit to carry it. That is also why he has never gone on — you cannot leave, he says, in the middle of a measurement. The flaw in the reasoning is not on his maps. It is in the man: he has mistaken carrying a thing alone for keeping people safe from it, and the ground is not slowing down.

cfe826c1.description: Priestess of a faith she no longer believes and cannot stop practising. Ask her and she will say so. Watch her hold a service and you will not believe her.

lore.t: The believing fell out of her somewhere on the crossing, and she will say so to anyone who asks, flat as a floorboard. Why she holds the services anyway is in
the Human Dead

, and it is the truth: the practice is a rota by another name, the candles are a fire, people come and stay and talk, and the talk is the thing. All of that she will admit in daylight. What she will not admit is what happens to her voice inside the service.

Ask her at the woodpile and the prayer goes to no one; ask her mid-liturgy and you would swear she had seen the answer. She never decided on the lie. It arrived like a work-skill, the way a smith's arm learns the blow: the old words want certainty behind them, and her body supplies it, and forty faces steady in the candlelight because the priest is sure. Last spring she sat with a friend at
Faded

— a woman losing the faces of her own children — who asked the bare question: will I be held? Jehanne heard her own voice say yes, whole and warm, not a splinter of doubt in it, and watched the woman settle under the word. It bought her a season. Jehanne walked home in the dark, was sick at the crossroads, and has never told anyone which part of the evening did that.

lore: She could go on; she is remembered whole by half the fireside, which is more than most can claim. She stays because the rota is short-handed, she says, and it is true, and it is not the reason. The reason is the forty faces. They believe her certainty, not her confession — and if she left, the leaving would tell them which one was real.

default_boy.description: Newly woken on the meadow with his name still on him, which is rarer than it sounds. What he was is over; what he will be has not been decided yet.

lore.t: He woke in the meadow grass with his name still on him, which is rarer than it sounds, and
Solveig

was beside him before the dew had soaked through his shirt. She told him the truth once, plainly, and asked his name and one true thing. The name came easily. The true thing took him until sundown — it was small, and she thanked him for it as if he had paid a debt, because here a true thing said aloud is exactly that.

lore: He still checks his pockets for something he last had on the other side. They are empty. So were everyone's — arriving with nothing is the one experience this whole country shares, and it is why a stranger here will feed you before you ask.

There is nothing remarkable about him, and this is not modesty: quick hands, a stubborn streak he had before the end, and no idea yet what either is for. Solveig is unworried. The ones who thank her, she says, always turn up at the meadow again sooner or later — on the far side of the courtesy, walking out into the wet grass to meet somebody new.

default_girl.description: Newly woken and hard to rattle. She had most of it worked out by the second evening, and has not yet said how she feels about any of it.
lore: She woke and took it better than most, which she is aware is a strange thing to be good at. By her second evening she had worked the rest out unassisted: that the fire was kindness rather than answers, and that the people being kind were not going to explain the important part, because they do not know it either. She has asked good questions ever since, and has not once asked whether it is really true.

lore.t: Bettany

came out from the stone house on her third morning, book open, the way she comes for everyone who will sit. The woman answered every question and then asked better ones back, which does not usually happen, and Bettany stayed past noon writing those down too. The last question, the gentle one — who she is waiting for — she was slowest to answer. What she said is not in the Chronicle; Bettany had already closed the book.

lore: What she is, is hard to rattle. Not brave the way the tellers mean it when they are working a room — brave in the flat, unremarkable way of somebody who looks at a thing that should be frightening, decides how frightened to be, and is then that frightened and no more. Everybody in this country is waiting for something. She has not said what. She will get around to it.

ef25b1f0.description: Scribe of the Chronicle — the book in your hands. She began it the day her grief went missing, and she will not close it until she knows what took it.

lore.t: Britt was the younger by six years and the quicker by every measure that is fun at a fair, and the sisters sang in parts — Britt above, Bettany under — through every wash-day of two lifetimes, the living one and this one. What happened when Britt went on is told in
the Long Morning
, and Bettany would rather you read it there. The short of it: everyone the going-on bereaves loses the grief itself, and everyone but her has agreed to call that mercy.
In the back of
the Chronicle

, past the last written page, there is a private column of dates. On Britt's day each year Bettany sings both parts of the wash-song alone, her line and then her sister's — she has lost none of it, which is the whole horror — and waits to feel anything at all, and writes the result beside the date. The column is longer now than some chapters. Every entry says: still nothing. She is a careful scribe. If it ever says something else, she wants to know the day.
She interviews everyone who will sit, and most sit once.
Wendell

gets her a whole evening every week and believes it is for his east road, which she has duly saved — forty pages, milestone by milestone. She keeps coming for a different reason. Wendell met Britt once, at a shearing, and he tells it a little differently each time — the dress, the weather, what Britt called across the pen — and Bettany sits very still through every version, waiting for the one with something new in it. He knows exactly what he is doing. He spins that morning out a thread a week, because the evenings are what he is really trading for; she pays, and both of them let the price go on being called the road.

amethyst_rune_soulstone.description: Faceted violet, plum deepening to lilac, with a thumbnail of gold at the middle that looks written rather than grown.

lore.t: Every facet on one is a one-off; the mark is not. Two strokes and a splayed foot, in gold, small enough to hide under a thumbnail, identical down to the stroke on every stone ever brought in. Off a creature that is
nothing but retellings

, the piece that pressed hardest was the one thing all its tellers' countries remember alike: gold, which does not drift. Set in a blade it lends tempo — the stroke arrives as if it had been made once already.
The mark is also why it is the most forged stone on any bench. Violet glass lumps well, and a forger with real gold gets the mark right every time, gold being the point of gold.
Osric
, new enough to still count in living years, bought one cheap off a stranger at his first market and carried it to
Sigrun

for setting. She drew it once through her hearth ash and handed it back grey. Ash will not sit on a true one — one wipe and it is finished — and the glass kept its coat. It hangs over his forge door now with the price scratched underneath, and he takes the ribbing better than he would take the sympathy.

banded_solar_stone.description: Dark stone terraced in bands, a seam of live gold running the length of them. It lights whatever pouch you put it in.
lore: The smiths' rule with this one: never on the bench after dark. The seam is live, and beside heated metal there is no telling the colour of the work from the colour coming off the stone, so settings happen at noon with the doors open, by people who otherwise keep their doors shut to read the heat.

lore.t: It does not go down when you put it away, which is why you cannot carry one and also arrive anywhere unannounced — and why, when the fire on the east road lapsed, its last keeper left a banded stone glowing on the sill as she went, so the road would think the light was still kept.
Wendell

walked that road while the trick still worked. He says you could tell a mile off, because a fire moves and a stone only glows. He stopped anyway, both ways, sat down on the step, and told it what he had seen on the road lately. It seemed wrong to pass a kept light without paying for it.
What bothers people is that it lends the whole light, undiminished, out of a lump a hand closes around. As if
the creature it comes off
was never lit through at all — as if the light was always this small, and the body was built around it for carrying.

black_egg_lava_veins.description: Charred black plates forked open by live orange veins that never cool. What you strike goes on burning after you stop.
lore: Ask somebody who carries one what they carry it in and you get a considered answer. Cloth chars through in a season; a pouch comes back stiff as a boot dried too near the hearth. Most end at a tin of sand lashed outside the pack, where the thing that cannot be persuaded to stop can do the least.

That is also what it does off an edge. Most fire is over when the swing is; this one is left behind, still burning after you step back. What got pressed to make it was never flame — it was the banking: heat held in, year after year, no fuel, no audience, no occasion. A thing like that does not learn to finish just because you have.

lore.t: Few ever come to hand, since a crossing has to empty first, and the one
Magmashell
anyone can still visit shows no sign of obliging. A collector once offered
Gunnar

good gold to stop paying its pause — one regular fewer, one crossing nearer done. Gunnar quoted back the number of years he has walked it, and the collector could not tell whether that was a price or a warning. Neither has anyone since.

brown_stone_egg.description: Dull brown plates shut on a copper vein, far too heavy for its size. A Puddling's last piece; in armour, hard to shift.
lore: The one they put in a new hand first. It weighs wrong — not heavy, wrongly heavy, in a way the arm reports before the eye agrees. Armour set with one does the same trick at scale: the blow that should have put you on your back leaves you standing where you were, and you find out afterwards. Wearers call it the least dramatic advantage in the trade, and keep wearing it.

lore.t: The trouble is the count. Every hard piece is supposed to be
the bottom of one long forgetting
, and the wet ground gives up more of these than the low country has lives to account for, by a margin that worsens every season.
Wendell
says that in his day the count came out even. Wendell says that about most counts.

lore: The sorters keep three explanations in stock. That the ground itself is doing the forgetting, and the wet places are where it runs deepest. That the counting was always sloppy. And a third, said late in the evening and not repeated in daylight: that the arithmetic is fine, and it is the assumption of one life to one stone that is wrong.

crimson_vein_mossy_stone.description: Moss green blotched with bark brown, dark veins branching in to one red knot at the middle. Filed with the blood stones.
lore: In a full bag you can find one without looking. Every hard piece is warm; this one is warm unevenly, a hot spot over the red knot at the middle, the way heat comes through a coat with somebody in it. Collectors mention that to each other exactly once, at the start, and not again.

lore.t: Every one of these on a bench was cracked out of
a Stumpling
by a hand other than
Sigrun's

; her refusal is its own story. What her bench shows is the other half of it: she will set the stones once the cracking is done elsewhere — sets them better than anyone in the district — and she lifts each one from the tray with the long tongs she otherwise keeps for iron out of the fire.

lore: An apprentice asked about the tongs once, it being a cold stone by iron's standards. It is warm in the middle, she said. They are all warm, said the apprentice, which is true. Not like this, she said, and got on with the setting, and the apprentice put the question away with the other things you do not ask Sigrun twice.

cyan_glacier_seam_stone.description: Grey plates split by one bright cyan seam that runs clean through. It bites frost, and what it strikes runs late.

lore.t: Warm, which is the first surprise — off the crystal ground, out of a shape that is ice from the crown down, and it sits in the palm at blood heat, the seam warmest of all. The sorters point to that when asked whether anything in a
Rimeshard
was ever under way at all: watched from a ridge it might as well be weather, and weather does not leave a warm stone.

lore: The grading is done on the seam, not on either material. Sight along it: on a good one the cyan enters one face and comes out the other, clean through. On a poor one it stops inside, and what you own is a grey pebble with a stripe. The rock alone is worth nothing; the ice alone is worth nothing; the join is the worth.

lore.t: New hands find that funny for about a week.
Osric

did not laugh at all. He is a smith; a join that outvalues both its pieces was the first price in this country that struck him as honestly arrived at, and he paid it without haggling, which the stone-sellers still bring up.

cyan_lightning_egg.description: Pebbled black under a net of branching cyan that will not sit still. Warm. Its spark rarely stops at one body.

lore.t: In the graders' register, the ground a stone comes off and the nature it grades to are two columns saying one thing — black rock, fire; high snow, frost. This is the line where the columns disagree: it comes down off
the Frostwraith
's snow, many days uphill, and it grades storm.
Gunnar
brings most of them down. He sells the stones readily and the places he found them not at all, which people take for a wanderer's habit, and which is actually arithmetic he does not like.

They fetch more than anything else off that mountain, and the first thing anyone learns fighting with one is not to let a friend stand at their shoulder: the spark goes where it is sent, and then sometimes it is in the next body along, whichever body that is.
Sigrun

will set one — for the price they carry she can hardly refuse — but she asks a single question first, who do you fight beside, and there are answers she hands the stone back over. Asked for her reasoning, she taps the head of her hammer and does not give it.

dark_grain_soulstone.description: Dark as bog oak, black grain running through the brown. A felled Sprigling's last: it stiffens plate and hands blows back.
lore: It will not take a polish and it will not be forced. There is grain in it, black under the brown, turning at a knot the way sawn oak turns, and an armourer sets a plate across the run of it or watches the first real blow start a split that does not stop. No other stone asks to be read first. Most of the trade finds that quietly insulting.

Worn right, it keeps a ledger: a share of every blow goes back to whoever gave it, at once, at about the size it was given, and the wearer feels nothing at all. Two exchanges in, the other party is usually looking at their own hands. Not protection — bookkeeping.

lore.t: Osric

ruined his first one the week he bought it, taking a smith's hammer to a thing that wanted a joiner's patience, and the two halves are nailed up over his forge door. Ask why he keeps them and you get the whole of what he will so far say about being dead: some things here are worked with, not on. Then he reads the next
Sprigling
stone a long while before touching it, like a man laying a floor.

gold_seamed_teal_soulstone.description: Sea-green, webbed with gold where it broke and broke again. It holds armour together, and gold has a way of turning up.
lore: Gold in the hand is always cold. The gold in this one is exactly as warm as the sea-green around it, and that detail still stops conversations. The mend is no setting, either: it runs the whole way through, filed and worked like trade goldwork, and it will not come out of the stone, nor the stone off it.

Handlers grade by the seams and argue the count — one school calls it a tally of seasons worked, the other says a stone is not a calendar. What the count means is not argued: this broke, and held, and broke again, and held. Armourers promise only that a plate carrying one comes apart later than it should, and often not at all. A stone that is mostly mend teaches a mend.

lore.t: Halvard
, the pedlar who walks his pack between the fires and
prices in nothing but gold
, will buy one, sell one, carry one — and book it as stone, never as gold: gold that cannot be spent is not gold to him. Pressed once, he weighed a
Palemaw

stone in his palm, said the difference between the two prices was the animal, and would not be drawn further. He does allow that carriers find more gold in a season than luck explains, and he counts his purse twice after trading with one.

green_venom_vein_stone.description: Cobbled grey plates, green standing wet in every joint. In a blade the poison layers on and never clears out.
lore: It travels alone, at the bottom of the bag, with something folded between it and the rest, because the green gets out — not much, never fast, never stopping. A pouch that has carried one for a season is marked inside for good. The crackers' rule is flat: you carry one of these, or you carry the rest.

lore.t: So somebody has to walk the green bag, and the somebody is
Jehanne

. She took the office unasked, the way she takes every office no one else wants, and walks a day behind the buying party with the bag on a pole over her shoulder, washing her hands at every stream, saying over each stone the blessing of a faith she tells everyone she no longer holds. The trade pays her in firewood. She has never once been robbed.
Graders can usually say inside a minute whether the thing in their hand is a fact, an appetite, or a habit. This one is none of the three. It is a substance — the same green
the Palehusk
leaks — and a substance is not a life pressed small. It grades high anyway. High enough that the question rarely gets asked twice.

grey_stone_crimson_veins.description: Cold grey plates with a warm red seam shut inside them. It gives nothing until you cut, and then it takes its share back.
lore: Buyers turn one to the light, hunting the gap where the red shows through. The crackers gave that habit up years ago — shut tight or on show, it is the same stone — and test with the fist instead: close it and wait for one warm line to come up against the palm, in a stone otherwise colder than the grass it came out of.

What it does begins half a breath after your first cut lands. Whatever you opened, some part of it comes back the other way and closes what it finds. Everyone who has felt it says the same two things in the same order: that it is a great deal of comfort, and that it is not a kindness. Nothing is being given. Something is being taken and divided.

lore.t: Gunnar
wears one wired in behind his belt buckle on the far rounds, through country the
Duskfang
still holds. Asked at the meadow fire what carrying it is like, he gave the question thought — which from Gunnar is a long answer already — and said: like being lent to. He did not say by whom.

hollow_black_soulstone.description: Cracked all the way through, with nothing in the cracks. What reached the bottom of this one was never its own.

lore.t: A soulstone is the bottom of a creature: one fact, one appetite, pressed to mineral. This one comes out of
Grinmask

cracked all the way through, and there is nothing in the cracks. Not damage — they all come out like that. The trade's working explanation is short and unpleasant: that shape was emptied long before anyone broke it, so what settled to the bottom of it was never the creature's own. It was the visitor's.
By that reading, everyone who carries one is carrying a fragment of
the thing under the mountain
. Several people have pointed this out. Nobody has stopped. The exception is
Hearn
, who has been nearer the source than anyone: he sold his the same evening it was paid to him, under its price, to a buyer he did not look at.

lichen_green_soulstone.description: Mottled olive crust over smooth grey, dark in the seams. A Mirewart's last piece; small hurts close as you walk.
lore: The commonest stone there is: dealers do not count them, they weigh them, and a bagful has bought a first winter's boots for a great many people who came to the fires with nothing else to sell. The trade calls it a walking stone — it works between places and never during. Carry one across a long day and there is no moment you feel it; at the fire, the day's small hurts have closed without ceremony.

lore.t: The part worth more thought is who keeps them. A great many people are still carrying the first one they ever took, years past affording better, and
Bettany
has been collecting their reasons for
the Chronicle

: it is lucky, it is paid for, it sits right in a pocket. She notes that not one reason quite holds, and that every keeper can still say exactly where the water was and how the light sat on it. The first thing a frightened newcomer breaks in this country is very often
a slow green weight
that did not run, and what they carry up from the mud is this. Kept, she has written, the way an apology is kept by people who would rather carry it than say it.

matte_black_shadow_stone.description: Matte black, softly faceted, handing back no light at all. In a full pouch you find this one by touch, not by eye.

lore.t: Stones are sorted on a dark cloth by lamplight, and every one says something on the way down — a coin of light, a stripe. This one lands and there is only cloth where it landed. Old hands still count the row twice before tying the bag. The fix is
Sigrun
's: any pouch that leaves her bench with one of these inside has a bright thread sewn to it, no charge, no comment. You check the thread.

Set in a blade it is the not-being-seen, finished and portable. Fights end, and the ending does not particularly include you: the shape goes down looking at somebody else. Off a creature that spent its whole loud life
charging head-first
, that is the stone's one correction — the charge was the noise. The bottom fact was never being looked at.

lore: Sigrun also keeps one loose in her apron, unset. A smithy is a place where people stand about and watch your hands, and on the days when the work on the bench is a cracking, she would rather the watching slid off.

mossy_green_egg.description: Dark green plates shut around a yellow-green star, and the moss on them is still growing. It cuts and it mends.
lore: The only piece that is still doing something. Set one on a shelf and leave it a year and the moss has got further — a plate's width up the shaded side, on a stone fed nothing and watered by nothing. People who handle stones by the sackful stopped finding that remarkable long ago, and still keep this one where they can see it.

The trade's one argument is where to put it, because the stone does not care. Growth goes into whatever it is set against: turned outward on an edge it opens a shape faster than the shape can close, worn against the ribs it closes the wearer while they are still being opened. Same work. It is not doing two things.

lore.t: Hearn

wears his sewn into the lining, ribs side, and has kept it there since before the mountain. His ruling on the argument is the longest sentence most people have got out of him: a thing that cannot tell cutting from mending, you keep on your own side of the fight. He paid
a Mosscairn's
fist for it, and calls the price fair, which from Hearn is a review.

mossy_root_stone.description: Dull olive under a dark web of root, plain enough to lose in the grass. Your cuts close over and your blows come up green.
lore: Stones are weighed by hand before they are weighed by scale, and the hand is hunting appetite: a piece off something that burned sits in the palm with a want that comes through a glove. This one sits there like a stone — matte olive, no shine, easy to lose in grass — and the trade priced it accordingly for years. Wrongly. The flattest ones are not empty; their want is pointed at something other than you.

lore.t: Carry one and the pointing shows: by evening the small hurts have closed unnoticed and the day's work has come apart readier than the edge explains. Everything else off a
Nightmule

is about a person who is not there. The stone alone is about the animal, and there is no owner in it at any depth — whoever walked at the front never reached the bottom. What reached the bottom was the going on, unloaded, in a straight line. That is the part in your pocket.

pale_bone_soulstone.description: Chalk-cream, crazed edge to edge with fine dark fissures, and not one of them gives. In armour it refuses to come apart.
lore: Hand one to somebody new and watch the thumb. The whole surface is crazed, fine dark fissures dividing the chalk-cream into panels like a flat of dried mud, and every pair of hands new to it presses, gently, to find out how near the thing is to coming apart. It does not give. The trade keeps a short demonstration for buyers who will not take that on trust, involving a bench and the flat of a hammer, and the stone wins.

lore.t: It stays cheap all the same, and the reason is honest: there is nothing to feel. In armour it pays out at the one moment you would otherwise not be getting up, and that is a hard thing to sell to anyone who has never been on the ground.
Solveig

keeps the fire the broken re-form beside, and has sat with what comes back — minus a little of what it was thinking — often enough to have a settled opinion. She gives every new bag-carrier heading out the same advice: past the bright stones, buy the dull one. The ones who laugh at the price have not been on the ground either. She says it pleasantly, once, and does not argue. Her fire will make the case for her some night, whichever stone they chose.

pale_sand_stone.description: Sun-bleached plates cracked round a heart of gold, all a Dewling leaves. Blows land like a dropped weight, and dazzle.
lore: Cutlers keep the seams turned outward, for the flash: whatever takes the hit stands blinking at nothing for a second, and there is no light anywhere about to account for what it thinks it just saw. Bedded the wrong way, it is merely heavy.

The sorters grade them by how little colour is left. A sand-brown one came off ground somebody still walks. The bone-pale ones, seams gone nearly white, come off meadows a great many people remember and none of them visit any more, and fetch double. A strange way to price anything; the trade stopped finding it strange long ago.

lore.t: Bettany
came to the sorting sheds last autumn and copied ten years of grade-books into
the Chronicle
, price by price, and would not say what she wanted them for. She did not need to. Anyone can read a column that only climbs: every season the
Dewlings
come up a little paler, off a few more meadows going unwalked.

pink_seam_granite_stone.description: Grey granite plates held by unbroken salmon-pink seams. In armour a crushing blow arrives as a shove, a fall as a bruise.
lore: It is not one piece, and that is the trade of it: grey granite plates held each to each by salmon-pink seams, so it holds the way a wall holds — by how it is joined. Struck along a seam it opens into two clean plates that both still work; struck across the grain, gravel. Reading the pink before the hammer falls is a living in itself.

lore.t: In armour it makes the ground feel closer: drops come off short, and what lands on you arrives without the part that was going to break something. The trade's sour rule holds here — stones off things that struck go into blades, and the stones that keep a person whole come off
a white creature
that never struck first in its existence, and spent the whole of it on one question: where to be standing when something heavy happens.
Hearn

wore one on the one organised walk anyone ever made on the cave. The others carried striking stones, and ribbed him the whole way east for armouring himself off a rabbit, and he let them. He came back alone, and unhollowed, and has never said whether the stone mattered inside. What is known is smaller: it has not been out of his plate since — not regraded, not repriced, not looked at.

purple_venom_claw.description: A purple hook with one pale ridge of light down the curve, and a hard green crust dried on the last third of the point.

lore.t: It grew where it sits — the one thing off an
Ashfiend

that did. Longer than a finger, curved well past use, the base a socket shaped around a knuckle that is not there any more. Hafted, it makes a poor knife every time, and people keep the poor knife, because a claw is worth little and a claw with a hand behind it is worth something.

lore: The crust on the point is the part worth money: mustard at its base, hard green at the tip, sitting on the purple rather than in it. It was put there; it did not grow there. It flakes under a thumbnail, so the careful carry one point-down in a stiff wrap and wash afterwards.

lore.t: Bettany
pays over the odds for a well-crusted one, and she is not buying knives. The same green comes off
the pale walking thing
on the black rock, and two creatures' leavings agreeing about a pigment is the kind of sentence
the Chronicle

exists to catch. Whether this point put the green into something or drew it out, the crust will not say. She keeps her best one wrapped in linen inside a chapter that has no words in it yet — just the claw, and a heading: which way did it run.

red_seam_pyre_stone.description: Dark plates split by live red, brightest where the seams meet. It never cools, and what it sets alight keeps burning.
lore: A bag of hard pieces can be sorted in the dark if one of these is in it. Every soulstone comes out warm; this one comes out well past warm and stays there, year on year, with nothing going in. Carriers keep it wrapped and away from their backs, because after a day of it you stop being able to tell which of you is the warm one.

Setters grade by depth, against a strong light. Red that stops at the skin of the plates lights what you strike and has done; red that runs down in keeps it lit after you have moved off and stopped attending. And it will not divide — split one along its own cracks and you hold two dark rocks and no fire — so the hilt is built around the whole of it.

lore.t: A cracker once offered
Jehanne

a deep one for her rota hearth: set it in, the fire never goes out, walk the circuit in half the nights. She refused it flat, and the refusal is the nearest she comes to a creed — a fire that keeps itself is not a fire. The stone can burn. It cannot sit with anyone. She walks the full circuit still, and the coal off
the crusted thing on the black rock
goes into sword-hilts instead, where burning past reason is a virtue.

rimed_blue_soulstone.description: Grey-blue plates, white rime in every seam, cold to hold. All a Frostling's melt leaves; its hits leave a target wading.
lore: The only cold hard piece. Every other kind sits at blood heat within a breath of being picked up; this one stays cold for as long as anyone has troubled to hold it, and the sorters use that as the test — blue junk warms in the hand while you are still asking after it, a real one never does.

lore.t: The price is not about the stone; it is about the walk. The high snow lies a long way above the last fire anybody still tends, and a collector broken up there — usually by the very
Frostling
they were working — comes back together beside the nearest fire still kept, which is most often
Solveig's
on the meadow, a full day's climb below the morning's collecting, still lying in the drift where it fell.

lore: Solveig has learned the look of it: somebody assembling out of the fire-warmth at noon with snow still in their idea of themselves. She puts the kettle on and does not ask. By evening, as a rule, they are talking about going back up. Not many go up twice in a season. She has never once asked the ones who do.

rusted_slit_stone.description: Near-black, slit all over, bright copper standing in every slit. Blows land harder and the armour that stops them fails.
lore: New hands rub the copper on a cloth, expecting the orange to come away. It never does — the first sign this is not rust in the ordinary sense — and it is warm, which rust is not. The trade grades on the copper regardless: bright, and running the full length of the slits, is a prime one; brown and pinched out is a dry one, and a dry one does noticeably less to the other man's armour.

lore.t: The odd part is that no two carry the same rust. One kind of animal, one kind of stone — there is no argument about that part — but one comes up coppery, one near black, one with a green in it, and the difference is not the animal. What pressed down in here is iron that was never its own: somebody's left-out things going off in the weather, year over year, beside
a small kept appointment
Wendell

was handed a green-tinged one at the fire a few winters back and turned it in the light a long time. The green, he said, was paint; he could name the gate it flaked off, and the wall the gate hung in. Then he talked until the fire was low, and for once — ask anyone who knows the old man — he named no price.

smouldering_dark_egg.description: Scorched near black, embers banked in every crack. A Slagling's last warmth: it warms the blade and the hide behind it.
lore: Most hard pieces go into the bag. This one goes into a pocket, and a great many never come out again: the seams stay lit, a low orange banked down in the cracks that has never yet been seen to go out. In a blade it is a poor bargain and the trade says so — the edge runs a little warm, and that is the whole of it.

lore.t: The quarrel about them is old and fair. A teller will point out that warmth is not
a fire

— a fire is warmth with somebody talking beside it — and the two ought not to be confused. The ones who walk the black rock, where the rota lapsed further back than anyone can date and the nearest tended fire is a day down the mountain, answer that up there a warm thing in the pocket is not an argument about anything. It is company.
Jehanne
keeps fires for a living and a
Slagling's
ember in her coat, so both sides of the quarrel claim her. She lets them. A woman who prays without believing has room, she says, to be right in both directions.

starlit_void_stone.description: Night-black, small lights all through it, pale seams branching over it that open into nothing. Lighter than it should be.

lore.t: Handlers grade stones by heft in the dark, and this one lies to the hand: night-black, full of small lights at no settled depth, and far too light for what it is. It is the dearest thing the eastern ground gives up, and it is paid for in
gold
only — for this one, no seller takes anything that drifts.
Osric
, who had been woken about a year and still thought like a living smith, reasoned that a stone which moves a fighter might move him out of harm's way, and set one into a breastplate.
Osric

, who had been woken about a year and still thought like a living smith, reasoned that a stone which moves a fighter might move him out of harm's way, and set one into a breastplate. It moved him one stride — into the middle of what he was backing away from. He re-formed beside
Solveig
's fire a night later, short the end of the argument he had been winning, and
Sigrun
pried the stone out of the dented plate, set it in a blade, and hung the plate on her wall where customers can see it.
In a blade, where it belongs, blows land heavy and dark, and once in a while the fight turns and you are standing on the far side of it, facing a back — the side
the Balefiend
was always on: the one you were not watching.

armor_tusker.description: Armor that grew instead of being forged. Spears skate off its plates; its tusks do not return the favor.

lore.t: Sigrun

calls it a cheat. Everyone laughs, and she is not joking. She has given a working life to the shoulder — the gap a plate harness has to leave so the arm can go up, and therefore the gap everything gets in through. Every smith who ever lived has failed at the shoulder. This animal wears bands that slide across one another when it breathes and shut when it turns, and it earned none of them, and does not know it has them.

lore: She has been out to look at one four times now, taking no tools, getting no nearer than she has to, standing there watching a beast breathe — the least Sigrun-like thing she does all year. The tusks curve out low and forward and they are built for lifting; what they lift is whatever was standing in front of it. She has not made a shoulder yet.

Understand what she is actually trying to build. Nothing out here can be ended with a spear, so people take plate for vanity. Sigrun has watched what a bad shoulder really costs: a person goes down, re-forms by the nearest fire some hours later, and comes back short a little of what they were thinking — a face, a stretch of road, a name that gave them no trouble last year. It is not a wound. It is a subtraction, it does not come back, and they turn up at her door afterwards unable to say quite why they came. That thing out on the plain has never lost one thought to a spear in its life. She goes back next week.

black_horse.description: A black horse that casts no shadow. It stamps, and the dark pools around its hooves like spilled ink.
lore: There is nothing whatever wrong with this horse. Sound feet, good coat, eats, sleeps, comes when it is called, hauls whatever you put behind it and does not sulk about the load. The only thing it does not do is lay a shadow on the ground. On a bright day people will watch the grass beside it for a while, and then find a reason to be somewhere else.

It has had a dozen owners and been handed on a dozen times, and every one of them offered a different reason out loud: too big for the yard, wrong temperament, no work for it this season. The reason none of them offered is that everybody knows which end of a long story a missing detail comes off, and a good horse you are going to have to stand and watch is worse than no horse at all.

lore.t: Sigrun

took it four years ago and has not handed it on. It hauls charcoal, stands in the yard behind the smithy while she works, and in the evening she scratches the place under its jaw it likes until it leans its whole considerable weight into her hand. People who know what she has already sat through in her life ask her, carefully, whether that is wise. She says the horse hauls charcoal.

blight_elk.description: The fungus steers the elk now. Its antlers bloom green in the dark, sowing spores wherever it grieves.

lore.t: Sporehorn keeps a circuit.
Gunnar

walked it out over two winters — he maps ground that will not hold still, and an animal that repeats itself was a rest — and got three stops: a ford, a burnt orchard, and a bare slope above the orchard with nothing on it at all. It stands at the ford a while. At the orchard a while. At the bare slope until the light goes.

There was a hut on that slope. Gunnar asked eleven people before he found one who could still say so, and she could not produce the woman's name — only that she kept goats and fed whatever came to the door, elk included. The hut is not there now, nor the track up to it. Things nobody tells about
go soft, and then go
, and that elk is the last thing in the world that still turns up.

lore: The fungus did not pick the route. It has only worked out where the elk stands longest, and standing still is the whole of what a fungus wants. The right antler is green through and wet with it; the left is still an elk's. The mushrooms come up thickest on the withers, the flat of the back, where you would put your hand on an animal to steady it. Gunnar's map marks the roads between as bad ground and will not say why. He says Sporehorn is no danger where it stops. It is a danger on the way, and he would rather people were not standing in the road when it goes to see about her.

butterfly_dragon.description: Wings exact to the last scale, a lantern-sized dragon guessed at, and a jet of flame three times its length.
lore: No dragon was ever anywhere to be remembered. What there was, in a hundred countries at once, was the telling of one, and a telling said often enough, to enough people listening, weighs as much here as a life does. So this is not the memory of an animal; it is the memory of an account, and you can see the difference at ten paces. Whoever did most of the remembering had never seen a dragon — no one has — but they had lain in a summer meadow once, watching the irises being worked over close up, and when the account ran out, that is what came to hand. The wings are the best-made thing on it: four of them, violet banded with pink, exact to the last scale. The body is a grey-green guess the size of a lantern. What got looked at came out sharp. What got taken on trust came out approximate.

lore.t: Osric

called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The fire is the one detail every retelling in every country kept, so it came through whole and unworn, entirely indifferent to the size of the thing carrying it.
Osric

, not yet a year woken and still sure of things, called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The tellers do his eyebrows when they tell it, and he sits and lets them, which is most of why the fire likes him. Being wrong about a creature does not make it harmless. It only decides which parts of it are.
Bettany
keeps a page of dragon accounts in
the Chronicle
and cannot get two of the woken to agree on wings, size, colour, or where the hoard was kept. The page carries one sentence every hand has signed. The fire is right.

chestnut_horse.description: A farm horse that outlived its farm. It still waits at the gate each dusk for a hand that never comes.
lore: The gate is still standing — two posts and a bar in open grass, the farm gone out from behind it. At dusk the horse comes up the slope, takes its place on the field side facing where the yard was, and waits about an hour to be brought in. The hand it waits for might be at a fire three days' walk from here, no longer able to tell you it ever owned a horse. It might never have woken at all.

lore.t: Osric

has been here three years and still counts in living ones, which is why he tried. He took it an apple; it ate the apple out of his hand very politely and went back to standing. He took it a rope; it walked with him most of a field, then turned round without any fuss whatever and walked back. He kept that up the better part of a season, in the hour after the forge was banked, which is not an hour a working man has spare.
Jehanne

watched one evening from the fence and told him to leave the animal be. She would not say why and did not have to; she keeps an appointment of her own at dusk, daily, and has known for years that there is nothing at the other end of it. What she did not tell him was the rest of it — that he had not been trying to move a horse.
Snowmane

has walked people past that gate more than once, at the shoulder of somebody who could not find their way in the dark, and it has never stopped there. It goes with the lost. Whatever else is wrong with the horse at the gate, it knows exactly where it is.

corrupt_stag.description: A thorn-racked stag so dark it reads as a gap in the wood. Violet light in its flank, and nothing regrows behind it.

lore.t: Jehanne

plants white bellflowers behind the chapel every spring, because the rite wants them and she has never found the trick of stopping. Thornstag comes in autumn, within a night or two of the same night, and takes the plot down to bare dirt. What it has browsed does not come up again — not that year, not after. She barrows the dead soil out and barrows new soil in, and she does it every time.

lore: Inside a lamp's throw of it, which she has been, you get very little. A stag-shaped hole in the dark. A rack too wide for the gap it just came through. A violet seam working in the break of its flank, thin light where ribs ought to be. It has no interest in her whatsoever. She could put a hand on it. She has not.

lore.t: Bettany

sat up with her one autumn to get the thing written down and came away with three pages on the stag and nine on the bellflowers, which tells you where the story is. Everybody says fence it. Jehanne has the wood. Jehanne has had the wood four years. She stopped believing a long time ago and could not stop practising; the fires have gone out across half the map; the rota is a courtesy nobody keeps. And that stag has not missed an autumn yet. Ask her plainly and she answers plainly: she would rather be robbed on schedule than left alone.

crystal_horn.description: A beast crowned with one great amethyst horn. It headbutts like a landslide and grazes on buried gems.
lore: Amethyrn never fell and never was anyone. Count instead the men who went into a hill certain — properly certain, the way you are certain of your own hand — that the next foot of rock had something in it, and count how many of them were wrong. Then work out what a few thousand years of that settles into, given nowhere to be and nothing else to do. It got up. It is the size of a cart, plated like a woodlouse, and it is never wrong.

The horn is one piece of amethyst as long as your forearm, and it is not the useful part. What the beast grazes comes back up through its shoulders in clusters, so a bull that has been feeding well is wearing the assay on its own back, and a patient man with a glass can read a whole hill from the next ridge. That is why people follow it. It headbutts like a landslide. That is why they follow it from the next ridge.

lore.t: Osric

has spent two years trying to reach a seam before it does and has not managed it once, which he considers unreasonable in a thing that walks slower than he does. He arrived recently enough to still count his age in living years. He is saving — in
gold
, the one substance here that does not drift — and has not yet worked out what for.
Wendell
pointed out, kindly, over a fire, that Osric has all the time there is. Osric said that was the worry.

crystal_lynx.description: A lynx grown through with crystal. Light bends wrong around it, and its tail-blade sings when it strikes.

lore.t: Sigrun

heard one before she saw it and put a hand out to stop the person walking next to her, which is not a thing she does. The tail-blade sings on the strike, one high note, the same note every time. In her trade that sound means a flaw running all the way through, and an edge that is going to let go, and the only open question is on which stroke. She stood in the trees a long while listening to an animal make the noise a bad blade makes, and could not manage to dislike it.

lore: The crystal comes up at the shoulders, the hips and the brow, and it is still coming. It sits heaviest on the joints, the worst place on an animal to put weight, so an old one moves like something much older than it is. You can find the rubbing rocks out in the crystal country: a smooth boulder with a scatter of snapped points around the base. That is grooming. It is trying to get something off itself that is itself. The same growth bends the light, so what you see stands a hand's width from where the lynx is, always to the same side, and hunters are taught to strike beside the animal and trust the correction over their own eyes. The ones who cannot make themselves do it come back saying it moved. It did not move. There is no account of one ever moving at that moment.

dark_donkey.description: Unharnessed, unloaded, unled — and still keeping to its route. Get in the way and it comes on at a walk.
lore: In the life it fell out of, somebody owned it. That is worth knowing, because of what comes off one: a bronze camp knife, hemp rope chewed to a splay, three iron links worn smooth on the inside by years of harness, a roll of coarse grey canvas. One person's kit for going somewhere and stopping for the night, all of it still coming off an animal that is carrying nothing at all.

lore.t: It keeps a route. It comes on at a walk, in a line, and the line does not bend around you, because you are standing in a road it was walking before the road went soft.
Wendell
swears the line is the old east road, and for an evening's company he will name you every stop on it — which is one more thing than the animal can do.

lore: The load went. The voice up at the front went so long ago there is no name left to put to it. Now and then it halts in open ground, swings both ears forward at nothing whatever, waits to be spoken to, and then walks on.

desert_cat.description: A cat armored in noon-light. Its golden scales drink the desert sun and pay it back in blinding flashes.

lore.t: More people have followed this cat than any other animal in Nangijala, and every one of them was following something it has not got. The plates look like gold, and gold is
the one thing everybody here agrees about
, so a person who has seen gold is certain about it in a way they are almost never certain about anything. In shade the cat is the colour of ordinary sand. Nothing comes off it. It is a cat.

lore: The flash is not a display, it is the entire defence. At noon it turns broadside, the plates take the sun and hand it back, and whoever is behind it loses their eyes for a count of ten, which is all it needs and all it ever uses. Early and late it hides instead, and hides well, because sand is what it actually is. The ones who get close go at dawn and stop expecting gold.

There was a man who followed one for eleven years. He gave up his work for it, walked out of two fires' rotas to do it, and got near enough four times to watch the plates dull over in shadow, which should have ended the business and did not. Asked what he meant to do if he ever caught the animal, he said he had stopped thinking about that part around year three. He was not a fool by then and he was not greedy. He had somewhere to be every morning, in a country where you can wake up and find you have nothing to do for the next four hundred years, and he had decided that was the better half of the bargain.

diablo.description: A crowned bone face, two sizes too big for the starved body carrying it. Fights head-first. Goes to ash.
lore: It does not walk. It gathers both feet under itself and crosses the ground in bounds, and it takes you crown-first, head down, the hardest thing left on it leading. Nothing that ever hunted for a living fights with its face. And it hurries. Everything empty in the open country has all the time there is; this one moves like something with an errand, and the errand is not its own.

lore.t: What comes off one is mostly not its own either. Grey talons of the kind the lit thing sheds. Hooks sized for a big cat's mouth. On
Sigrun
's bench last autumn, out of a head with two red eyes, a whole wet eye, brown.
Osric
, new enough to still ask things out loud, asked what it wanted the eye for. Sigrun tied the bag and put it with the others. Everyone in the room understood the answer except him.
Broken, it folds at the knees and settles, and the settling is ash; the wind has the heap by morning, near
the mouth
as anywhere. It leaves no mask. The face goes with the rest of it — it only goes last.

diablo_2.description: Nothing behind the face — four slit eyes burning in black stone, wreathed in dark. Its attack is to fall on you.
lore: A face of black stone, four slit eyes lit orange down it, red marks cut above and below them, the whole thing hanging inside a wreath of slow dark that takes fire when it moves. It does not strike. It rises, and it comes down on you with everything it weighs, meaning to crush. And the eyes shut first — all four, a breath before the stone cracks — so whatever was doing the looking is gone before the breaking starts.

lore.t: There are two accounts of it and neither has won. One: it is a shell the emptying made when it had nothing left to work with, the outside done beautifully, the inside not attempted. The other: it is one of the masks, left lying too long near
the mouth
, and no longer an object. The crackers prefer the first. The second has a next question in it.
Jehanne

was sent a rubbing of the red marks, on the reasoning that a priestess reads things. She kept it through a winter. In spring she burned it, and told the sender the marks say nothing at all — in the voice she keeps for the prayers she no longer believes. She has not gone east since.

dune_digger.description: It swims through sand the way fish forget water. Only the jagged back-plates betray the tide beneath.
lore: The dunes are the one ground in this country that keeps nothing. Put a thing under them and the sand hands it back — a week later, a season later, standing on end in a clean hollow with a delver's wake still settling around it. The animal is not looking for your box. There is nothing on the front of it that is looking at anything; it goes through a dune the way something goes through water, on those pale spade-claws, and whatever was down there ends up on top.

lore.t: Jehanne

walked three days east of her rota last autumn and buried the bell she calls people to fire with. She tells the story herself, at her own fire, and tells it well: how she could not go on ringing a thing she had stopped believing in, and could not bring herself to break it either, and so put it under a dune and came home lighter than she had walked out. Eleven days. Then a charcoal burner turned up at her door with it, upright and clean and pleased with himself.

lore: She rings it every evening now, and the story gets its laugh, and she lets it. What she leaves out is that anyone who has worked that country knows exactly what the dunes do with anything you put in them. She had been out there before. She chose the place.

eldritch_maw.description: It has no face, only appetite. The ringed mouth opens wider than reason, and the light goes in first.
lore: Look at the body before you look at the mouth. Four legs, a working shoulder, a tail with a switch in it — the whole frame of something that once grazed and was nervous of dogs. Then the neck ends in rings of teeth around a hole, and there is no face on it anywhere, no part of the head a name could ever have gone into. Violet marks crawl over the hide and give off their own light. Ordinary light goes the other way: hold a torch out toward one and it lights your hand and nothing past it.

There are three words for what a creature is here and not one of them will sit on this. It did not come — nothing that grazed anywhere arrives shaped like that. It was not made; the made are pooled out of what crowds of the dead agree on, and there is no crowd anywhere that agrees on this. And Hollowed means a thing emptied out and left with its outside, the outside being the whole of what the Hollowed keep. This one did not keep a face. The guides file it under Hollowed because a guide has to put a thing somewhere, and the crackers who work that ground will tell you plainly that the guides are guessing.

lore.t: Hearn
does not discuss
the mountain

. Everyone knows why and everyone asks anyway. Shown an account of one of these, he broke his own rule for it: not the mountain's work, he said, and then a second sentence nobody had asked for — that the thing under the mountain wants something, and this wants nothing at all, it only opens. He would not go further. His reason was never the Chronicle. People who believe a thing came out of the mountain go east after it, and Hearn has been east once, with company, and does not mean to be why anyone goes again.

forest_poring.description: Round and sand-pale, balancing one bright drop on a stalk. The drop is the weapon and comes round like a flail.
lore: The collectors call all the round ones lings, one word for the same business turning up in five kinds of country, and the low country's is pale as dry sand, holding a single bright drop up over itself on a stalk. Of everything a wet field at first light contains, the drop on its stem with the sun inside is the detail everyone keeps exactly; the rest wears down under all that remembering to pale grain, no particular grass, no particular year.

lore.t: It swings the drop round like a weight on a line, catching the light as it comes, meaning none of it. The trade's one rule is to work with the sun at your back, because whoever is looking into the flash when the blow lands loses the next few steps of the fight. Flattened, it leaves no body at all, just
something sun-bleached and far too heavy
lying in the pressed grass.
Most mornings one comes partway up the rise toward the fire on
the meadow where everyone wakes
and stops just short of the light, and the fire's oldest joke is that it has come to be met.
Solveig

lets the joke stand. But after a night when the fire sat ready and the meadow stayed empty, she has been seen walking down the wet field to stand beside it a while, and whatever she says there she has never once brought back up the hill.

forest_poring_2.description: Green, damp, a shoot coming up out of its head, and a little wooden sword in a fist it does not really have.
lore: The wood's ling is green and damp, with a live shoot coming up out of its head. A wood, to nearly everyone who ever remembered one, is a place you went into to take something out of, and the stroke is the part that comes back identical from every rememberer — so it carries a small pale-wood sword out of nowhere in particular and swings it at travellers and passing birds with the same blank willingness. No grudge; there is nothing in it that could hold one.

lore.t: Osric

burns charcoal at the wood's edge, and in his first month here — he still said weeks then, as if weeks were load-bearing — one walked its round through his camp every day and swung at him every time. What offended him was not the swinging but the grip. He stopped dodging, took the little fist it does not really have, and set the sword properly in it, the way you set an apprentice's. It struck him anyway. He maintains it struck better.
Broken, it is chips before you can regret it, small green pieces in all directions at once, and what stays behind is
a stone with black grain run through it like sawn timber

. Osric buys those from the woodcutters. His own one still comes through the camp, and he has moved the woodpile out of its road, and he does not say what he will do on the morning the round comes through empty.

granite_bear.description: A hillside that stood up. Moss and granite shift when it breathes, and climbers swear the mountain growled.
lore: Every valley had its one hill, and the people in it agreed on that hill's shape the way they agreed on almost nothing else: the same dark line against the same evening, seen from the same doorway, for generation after generation. And every hill of that kind carried the same story — there is a bear up there, do not go up after dark, I mean it. A hundred valleys' worth of that, held identically by everybody who ever lived in sight of one, and it does not stay a hill. The story stood up and brought the hill with it.

lore.t: Moving costs it. The seams open green down its legs when it walks and the moss tears along the shoulders, so mostly it declines to, and holds one position for years while people treat it as exactly what it looks like. There was a rota fire on the western rounds kept in its lee for eleven winters — out of the weather, with a wall at your back you could lean on all night. One spring the wall left. The keeper lost the fire twice to the wind before morning and finished the shift anyway, talking to whoever came, in the open, with nothing behind her.
Solveig
has a private word for keepers who do that. She has never once said it to their faces. The wall is somewhere further west now, standing still again, with eleven winters of soot up one flank.

gray_brute.description: It gnaws boulders to keep its tusks short. When the grinding stops, something softer has wandered close.
lore: You find the stones a long time before you find the animal: boulders worn into a shallow saddle, glassy in the dip, three or four of them to a clearing. A teller once copied the grooves off one convinced they were writing, and got as far as ruling out four alphabets before somebody who had actually seen a brute took pity. They are teeth-marks. It grinds its tusks down on rock, all its life, on purpose.

lore.t: Ask why an animal would file off its own best weapon and the answer is standing somewhere east, and has been standing there a very long time. A full-grown pair of tusks is a challenge, and there is only one thing in this country worth challenging, and
the old bull
has never lost. So they grind. Every young brute alive spends its whole span wearing itself smaller so it will not have to go and find out.

lore: Almost everything else out in that country is at Habit by now, walking a round with the animal long since gone out of it. Not this one. It is entirely present — it is frightened, it is deciding, it grinds — and being present is precisely what the fear costs it. So watch the stones. When the wear on one goes grey and weathered and no fresh cut appears on it for a season, something has been settled out there, and it is a long walk east.

gray_brute_2.description: The old bull of the brutes. Whole warbands have broken against shoulders wider than their shield-wall.

lore.t: There was an age here with enough people in it, and enough agreement between them, to put a shield-wall in a field and walk it forward in step. Sit with that fact by itself for a moment; it is a larger thing to know about this country's past than anything the animal ever did. Then note that the wall is the part that broke. The bull is out there yet, old past any counting, uninterested. It does not grind its tusks and has not needed to for longer than anyone can account for, and
the young ones
file theirs off rather than come and ask. So no one asks. It moves when it wants the sun.
Hearn

will tell you about that field. Hearn will tell you about it at length: the frost in the ground, the order the flanks went in, the sound a shield-wall makes at the moment it stops being a line and becomes people. He was not there — it was long before him — and he has every yard of it from those who were, and he can hold a fire for a whole evening with it, generous and exact and warm. It is not the story anybody sat down for. They sit down because Hearn went into the mountain with a party and came out of it by himself, and because he once said, of the inside, that it asked politely, and has said nothing since. So he gives them Tuskmaul. He gives them Tuskmaul every single time, and they take it, and they come back next week and take it again.

hedgehog.description: Still laying in stores for a hand that stopped coming. Crowd this brown handful of spines and the quills stay in.
lore: It travels the bottoms of things — walls, hedge-lines, the low sides of paths — on a route that stopped leading anywhere long ago, carrying a fistful of hard glossy kernels it cannot eat and will not be parted from. A hedgehog has no use for a nut. Behind this one was a person who put food out at a certain hour, and an animal that learned to be at the place when they did, and of that whole arrangement the piece that lasted is the being-there. It still arrives at the old hour, to a patch of grass where a doorstep used to be, and waits, and eats nothing, and moves on.

lore.t: Wendell

says the wall it keeps to on the old east road was a garden wall, and that he knows whose garden. He is not making it up; the road is his stock in trade, and he sells what he remembers of it for company. So the name this animal has been keeping its appointment with is not gone. It is sitting in an old man by a fire, one evening's listening from being said aloud, and nobody has paid the evening yet.

Crowd it and the quills go in barbed and stay in. Somewhere in the dark there is a black-pelted thing carrying three of them, from a meeting on the low side of a path that neither of them chose or understood. The
white rabbit
keeps an hour of its own, out on open ground. The low country is full of them.

hellhound.description: A hound cracked open by its own fire. Embers sift from its seams, and its howl smells of burning.
lore: A drover on the west road watched one for eight nights from his fire, then went down and walked it into the river. It let him. That is the part he tells badly every time and the part that costs him his sleep: a lean black dog standing chest-deep in cold water while a stranger poured more of it over the split seams along its ribs — steaming, patient, entirely willing — and the orange in the splits never dimmed by a shade. Then it came out, shook itself, and followed him up the bank.

lore.t: So he walked to
Sigrun

's door and asked her to release it. She went and looked at it for an afternoon, which is more than she gives most requests, and came back and said no, and gave him the reason in the two flat words of
her trade

. She cracks shapes that are thinning. This one is not thinning. It is holding beautifully — flame at the tail, fire between the ears, embers going out one by one on the ground behind it, every bit of it as steady as the day it arrived. What he wanted done would have been done for him, and she does not do that work for the watcher. She told him to stay off the road after dark. He goes. He reports that it waits for him at the same bend now, at the same distance, burning quietly, and that he talks to it. She has stopped telling him not to.

ice_crystal_golem.description: Dark rock grown through with ice: a crown, a mouthful, bladed arms, and more torn out of the ground at need.
lore: Above the snow line the ground turns crystal and stays that way, and the Rimeshard is what that ground does to a rock that stands in it long enough: dark plates iced through, a crown of blades off the skull, a mouth that is a row of them. When it wants more than it is wearing, it reaches down and tears it out of the ground — up there it and the ground are the same material, and there has never once been a shortage.

So the trade keeps one rule about it, bought dear and given away free: never above the line. Baited downhill onto ground that is merely ground, it spends its crown, then its shoulders, and cannot reach for more, and a patient crew can break the shape by dark. Above the line you are not fighting a creature so much as the ground it stands on, and the ground goes down a long way further than your patience.

lore.t: Ask
Hearn
what was under
the mountain

and he goes somewhere behind his own face. Ask him instead about the Rimeshard he passed on the trail down and he will talk all evening: how it marked him, and let him by, and wanted nothing, took nothing, asked him for nothing. He calls it the most restful thing on that whole road. People who work the high ground use the same word, restful — and use it, as a rule, in the season before they come down for good.

ice_poring.description: Packed snow with two dark eyes, heavier than snow should be. Every spike it throws is grown out of itself.
lore: Down in the grass the ground wanders; high under the crystal country nothing has needed correcting in a very long time, and there is hardly anyone left up there to walk on it. Out of ground held that hard comes the high snow's ling: snow pressed into a shape with two dark eyes, far heavier than snow has any business being, and armed entirely out of itself. A spike grows up through its crown and flies, and there is measurably less creature afterwards. It will do that until it cannot.

lore.t: Gunnar

goes up each year to check his measurements of the Drift against the one country that never moves, and each year the same one — the eyes set a little crooked; you learn one the way you learn a face — meets him at the last ridge and throws everything it has. He stands out of range and lets it finish. His is the only footfall on that road all year. Whatever it is armed against, he is the whole of what ever arrives.

lore: It is smaller each year. He measures it — he measures everything — and keeps the number where he keeps the rest, to himself. They do not shatter at the end; they slump, into slush inside their own footprint, and the wet mark outlasts them by an hour. Gunnar says that the year it does not throw at him, he will retire the route. He says it the way he says most things, so that you cannot tell whether it is a joke.

ice_wolf.description: Its mane is a crown of ice that never melts. The cold arrives a breath before it does, and stays after.
lore: You get the number before you get the animal: the fire wants twice the wood. Then it is at the rim of the light, heavy through the shoulders, a crest of ice grown up out of its neck like a crown hammered on wrong, icicles off the jaw, ice standing out through the claws. It does not come in. It has never once come in.

lore.t: Jehanne
